open_points.subject: refusal stage reporting
open_points.text: the number of each of A04 rule 6's six stages, which every refusal of a check carries (A04, owner, 2026-11-17)
open_points.question: Which module owns adding the stage number to a refusal, where in the refusal contract it appears, whether callers receive it or it is internal metadata, and whether “every refusal” means only failures of A04 rule 6 or every check elsewhere in Registry?
options: Every operation refusal returned to a caller has a public stage-number field, produced by a shared refusal/transport module
The stage number is internal refusal metadata and is not returned to callers
Only refusals produced by A04 rule 6 carry it; startup, upload and backup check failures do not
Every failed check in Registry, including startup and background work, carries it
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a public field on operation refusals only, owned by the shared operation-response layer; startup diagnostics and background failures do not use it.

witness.initial: A registered agent session has no grant for project P, and P exists; another id Q does not exist.
events: Cabinet Kernel calls the same project operation first with P and then with Q.
outcomes: An implementation returns refusal stage 2 for both calls as part of the external response.
An implementation keeps the stage internally and returns the existing indistinguishable not-found response with no stage field.
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel and the agent-visible operation binding

open_points.subject: completeness of the data closure's initial ordinal constants
open_points.text: the first revision of a Project and of a Customer (State 1, "an ordinal starting at 1") and an agent session's first access version (A12 rule 1).
open_points.question: Why are these initial ordinals release constants while the pointer version's first value, the audit sequence's new-store value 0 and consequently its first entry number are not named in the data closure, despite this module claiming to be the one home of every generated-code value outside settings, enumerations and field types?
options: Add exported constants for the pointer-version start and audit-sequence initialization alongside REVISION_FIRST and ACCESS_VERSION_FIRST
Declare that pointer and audit sequence starts are model/store invariants owned by their implementing modules, and state why revision and access-version starts are different
Treat all ordinal starts as model or field-type facts and remove REVISION_FIRST and ACCESS_VERSION_FIRST from data_provider
open_points.default_guess: Add POINTER_VERSION_FIRST and AUDIT_SEQUENCE_INITIAL constants to data_provider, deriving the first audit entry by incrementing the latter.
